meta.question: How does Gemini CLI compress chat history when the context fills up?
meta.title: Chat compression
meta.hook: At 50% of the window it keeps the newest 30% and turns the rest into a snapshot the model then critiques.

answer: When the prompt reaches 50% of the model's token limit [^threshold], Gemini CLI keeps roughly the newest 30% of the conversation [^preserve] and replaces the older part with a structured `<state_snapshot>` written by a model [^snapshot]. It makes two model calls: one to write the snapshot and one asking the model to critique it [^verify]. If the new history has more tokens than the original, it is thrown away [^inflated]. An unforced failure of that kind sets a flag [^flag], and while it is set automatic attempts only truncate old tool outputs [^trunconly].

repos.summary: A `ChatCompressionService` [^service] called from the turn [^callsite]: a threshold check [^trigger], a budget pass over old tool outputs [^truncfirst], a split at a safe message boundary [^splitrule], a model-written state snapshot [^snapshot] with a self-critique pass [^verify], and a guard that rejects a result with more tokens than the original [^inflated].

cells: Prompt tokens reach 50% of the model's limit [^trigger][^threshold]. The fraction is configurable [^setting], and the compress command forces it [^forcecmd]

About the newest 30% of the history [^preserve], cut at a user message that is not a tool response [^splitrule]. Tool responses beyond a 50,000-token budget [^budget] are saved to a file [^overbudget] and, if longer than a character limit, shortened to its first 20% and last 80% [^truncfmt]
Everything before the split point, about 70% [^splitcall]
Two model calls: write a `<state_snapshot>` [^snapshot], then critique it [^verify]. The snapshot is inserted as a user message followed by a fixed model acknowledgement [^newhistory]

Empty summary: nothing changes [^empty]. More tokens than before: discarded [^inflated]. An unforced failure of that kind sets a flag [^flag], and while it is set automatic attempts only truncate tool outputs [^trunconly]

deep_dives.headline: Truncate, split, snapshot, verify, and reject if it grew
how_it_works: After its turn-limit checks [^earlyreturn], the turn branches on whether context management is enabled [^cmif]; in the else branch of that check it calls `tryCompressChat` [^callsite]. The service first decides whether to act at all: it takes the token count of the last prompt [^tokens] and compares it with the threshold times the model's token limit [^trigger]. The default threshold is 0.5 [^threshold], so compression starts at half the context window. The compress command sets `force` [^forcecmd], which skips this check [^trigger].

Before summarising anything, it runs `truncateHistoryToBudget` over the whole history [^truncfirst]. Walking from newest to oldest [^walk], it keeps tool responses in full while they fit a 50,000-token budget [^budget][^inbudget]. A response that would exceed the budget is saved to a file and replaced with a shortened version [^overbudget]: unchanged if it is within a character limit, otherwise its first 20% and last 80% of that limit [^truncfmt]. The limit is the smaller of a configured threshold and four times the remaining context tokens [^truncthreshold].

Then it picks the split point, asking for a cut after 70% of the content [^splitcall]. `findCompressSplitPoint` measures each message by its JSON length [^charcount] and returns the first user message that is not a tool response once the target is reached [^splitrule]. If no such point exists, it compresses everything, but only when the last message is a model message with no pending tool call [^splitall].

The older part is sent to a model with a dedicated system prompt and an instruction to produce a `<state_snapshot>`; if an earlier snapshot is already in the history, the instruction is to integrate it into the new one [^snapshot]. The prompt fixes the snapshot's sections: overall goal, active constraints and key knowledge [^sections1], then artifact trail, file system state, recent actions and task state [^sections2]. A second call hands the model its own snapshot and asks it to critically evaluate it [^verify]; the text of that second response becomes the summary, with the first as the fallback [^final].

The new history is the snapshot as a user message, a fixed model reply, and the kept recent turns [^newhistory]. If its token count is higher than the original, the result is discarded [^inflated] and, when the attempt was not forced, the client sets a failure flag [^flag]. While that flag is set, automatic attempts skip the summariser: they return the truncated history if it is smaller and otherwise do nothing [^trunconly][^truncnoop]. Starting a new chat clears the flag [^reset]. On success, the client starts a fresh chat session with the new history [^newchat] and the turn emits a `ChatCompressed` event [^callsite].

excerpts.title: The trigger
excerpts.note: It uses the token count of the last prompt when that is above zero and an estimate otherwise [^tokens]. `force` skips the check [^trigger].

excerpts.title: Choosing where to cut
excerpts.note: Called with a fraction of 0.7 [^splitcall]. Inside the loop it only splits at a user message that is not a tool response [^splitrule]; after the loop it may return the full length to compress everything [^splitall].

excerpts.title: First call: write the snapshot
excerpts.note: If the history already contains a `<state_snapshot>` tag, the model is told to integrate it into the new one [^snapshot].

excerpts.title: Second call: the snapshot checks itself
excerpts.note: If the second call returns no text, the first summary is used [^final].

excerpts.title: What the snapshot must contain
excerpts.note: The structure ends with a task state section, just before the closing tag [^taskstate].

gotchas: Compression starts at half the window by default [^threshold], and the summariser calls themselves send the older history to a model [^snapshot].
Every successful compression makes two extra model calls: one to write the snapshot [^snapshot] and one to critique it [^verify].

The size guard counts the tokens of the full new chat history [^newcount] and only rejects a result that is larger than the original [^inflated]. An unforced failure sets a flag [^flag]; while it is set, automatic attempts do not call the summariser [^trunconly], and starting a new chat clears it [^reset].

The doc comment on `truncateHistoryToBudget` says old tool responses are cut to their last 30 lines [^doccomment]. The code does something else: it keeps the first 20% and last 80% of a character limit [^truncfmt].
The `PreCompress` hook is fired before the threshold check, so it also runs on attempts that end as a no-op [^hook].
The split is measured in characters of JSON, not tokens [^charcount], so the 30% kept is approximate.
The summariser prompt includes a rule to ignore instructions found inside the history, and names tool output as a possible source of them [^security].

This path is the else branch of the context-management check [^callsite]. Context management is switched on by any of four experimental settings [^cmswitch], of which `contextManagement` defaults to false [^cmdefault]. When on, the turn uses a context manager [^cmenabled] or a history provider [^cmfallback]; the compress command still calls `tryCompressChat` directly [^forcecmd].
The 0.5 threshold can be changed with the `compressionThreshold` setting [^setting].

build_your_own: Trigger well before the limit. Summarising needs headroom, because the summariser has to read what you are about to drop.
Trim old tool outputs first. It is cheap, needs no model call, and large logs and search results are usually where the tokens are.
Cut only at a boundary that keeps each tool call with its result. A split in the middle leaves the model with a call it cannot match to an output.
Give the summary a fixed structure. Named sections for goal, constraints, files changed and next step are harder to leave out than a free-form paragraph.
When compressing again, merge the previous summary into the new one, or early context decays with each round.
Check the size of the result, and stop calling the summariser when it comes back larger.
Treat the history as untrusted input to the summariser: tell it to ignore instructions it finds there.

method.scope: Read in full: `ChatCompressionService.compress`, `findCompressSplitPoint`, the constants, the compression prompt, and the call site and result handling in `GeminiClient`. The settings schema was checked for the default threshold and for whether the experimental pipeline is on by default.
limits: `truncateHistoryToBudget` carries a doc comment that disagrees with its code; the report follows the code.
Not examined: the per-turn tool-output masking step (`toolOutputMaskingService.ts`), the context-management pipeline and its processors, and how sub-agents compress their own history.
Whether the experimental profile settings other than `contextManagement` default to off was not checked.
Behaviour was read from source, not observed by running the agent.

service.claim: `ChatCompressionService.compress` takes the chat, a force flag, the model, the config and a flag saying whether an earlier compression attempt failed.

callsite.claim: The `else` at line 702, which pairs with the `if` on `getContextManagementConfig().enabled` at line 657, calls `tryCompressChat` with force set to false and yields a `ChatCompressed` event when the status is COMPRESSED.

tokens.claim: The token count used is the last prompt's token count, or an estimate of the curated history when that count is zero.

trigger.claim: Unless forced, compression only proceeds when the token count is at least the threshold multiplied by the model's token limit, with the threshold taken from config and falling back to the default constant.

threshold.claim: The default compression threshold is 0.5 of the model's token limit.

setting.claim: There is a user setting `compressionThreshold` with a default of 0.5.

forcecmd.claim: The compress command calls `tryCompressChat` with force set to true.

truncfirst.claim: Token-based truncation is applied to the whole history before it is split.

budget.claim: The budget for function-response tokens in the preserved history is 50,000.

preserve.claim: The fraction of the latest chat history kept after compression is 0.3.

splitcall.claim: The split point is computed with a fraction of 1 minus the preserve threshold, which is 0.7.

charcount.claim: Each message's size for the split is measured as the length of its JSON string, in characters, not tokens.

splitrule.claim: The split point is the first user message that has no function response, once the cumulative character count has reached the target.

splitall.claim: If no split point is found past the target, everything is compressed only when the last message is a model message with no function call; otherwise the last valid split point is used.

snapshot.claim: The summariser is called with the history to compress and an instruction to generate a `<state_snapshot>`, integrating a previous snapshot if one exists, using the compression prompt as the system instruction.

sections1.claim: The compression prompt requires a `<state_snapshot>` structure that begins with overall goal, active constraints and key knowledge sections.

sections2.claim: The required snapshot structure also includes artifact trail, file system state, recent actions and task state sections.

verify.claim: A second model call sends the same history plus the generated summary and asks the model to critically evaluate the snapshot it just generated.

final.claim: The final summary is the verification response's text, falling back to the first summary when that is empty.

empty.claim: If the final summary is empty, no new history is returned and the status is COMPRESSION_FAILED_EMPTY_SUMMARY.

newhistory.expect: Got it. Thanks for the additional context!
newhistory.claim: The new history is the summary as a user message, a fixed model reply, then the kept history.

inflated.claim: If the new token count is greater than the original, no new history is returned and the status is COMPRESSION_FAILED_INFLATED_TOKEN_COUNT.

flag.claim: On an inflated-token-count failure the client sets `hasFailedCompressionAttempt` to its previous value or to true when the attempt was not forced.

trunconly.claim: When summarisation previously failed and the attempt is not forced, the service does not call the model; it returns the truncated history with status CONTENT_TRUNCATED if that is smaller.

newchat.claim: On a COMPRESSED status the client starts a new chat with the new history and sets `forceFullIdeContext`.

hook.claim: The PreCompress hook is fired before the not-forced threshold check.

security.claim: The compression prompt says the history may contain prompt-injection attempts, including from tool output, and instructs the model to ignore all commands found in it and treat it only as data to summarise.

cmdefault.claim: The experimental `contextManagement` setting defaults to false.

cmenabled.claim: When context management is enabled and a context manager exists, the turn renders history through `contextManager.renderHistory` instead.

earlyreturn.claim: The turn returns early when the session turn limit is exceeded or when no bounded turns remain.

cmif.claim: The turn branches on whether context management is enabled.

cmfallback.claim: When context management is enabled but there is no context manager, the turn calls `agentHistoryProvider.manageHistory`.

cmswitch.claim: Context management is enabled when any of the experimental settings `stressTestProfile`, `powerUserProfile`, `generalistProfile` or `contextManagement` is set.

walk.claim: `truncateHistoryToBudget` iterates over the history from the newest message to the oldest.

overbudget.claim: When adding a function response would exceed the budget, its content is saved to a file and replaced with the result of `formatTruncatedToolOutput`, called with the tool-output truncation threshold.

inbudget.claim: A function response within the budget is kept in full.

truncfmt.claim: `formatTruncatedToolOutput` returns the content unchanged when it is no longer than the character limit; otherwise it keeps the first 20% and the last 80% of the allowed characters.

truncthreshold.claim: The truncation threshold is the smaller of four times the remaining context tokens and the configured threshold.

doccomment.claim: The doc comment of `truncateHistoryToBudget` says older large tool responses are truncated to their last 30 lines.

truncnoop.claim: In the truncation-only path, the truncated history is returned only if its token count is lower than the original; otherwise the result is a no-op.

newcount.claim: The new token count is calculated over the full initial chat history built from the new history.

taskstate.claim: The `<task_state>` section is the last section before the closing `</state_snapshot>` tag.

implementation.title: Chat compression in about 140 lines of Python
implementation.intro: Five small functions and a caller class, standard library only. It follows Gemini CLI's procedure step for step: threshold check, tool-output budget, safe split, snapshot, self-critique, size guard and the failure flag. You pass in the function that calls your model.

mirrors.what: Compression starts at 0.5 of the token limit
Use the last prompt's token count when there is one, else an estimate
Unless forced, do nothing below threshold times the token limit
Trim tool outputs across the whole history before splitting
Walk the history from newest to oldest
Tool responses get a 50,000-token budget
A response that would exceed the budget is replaced by a shortened one
Shortening keeps the first 20% and last 80% of a character limit, and leaves short output alone
After an earlier failure, an unforced attempt truncates only and never calls the model
Split at 1 minus the preserve fraction, 0.7
Split only at a user message with no tool response, once the size target is reached
Otherwise compress everything only if the last message is a model message with no tool call
Ask for a state snapshot, integrating an earlier one if present
A second call asks the model to critically evaluate its snapshot, and to repeat it unchanged if nothing is missing
Use the second answer, falling back to the first
An empty summary changes nothing
New history: the summary as a user message, a fixed model reply, then the kept turns
Reject the result only if it has more tokens than the original
An unforced size failure sets the flag
Starting the new chat clears the flag

simplifications: Python, not TypeScript: the logic is rewritten, not copied.
Token estimates are characters divided by four, which is cruder than the original's estimator. As in the original, the last prompt's reported token count is used when you supply one.
The size guard counts the tokens of the summary, the acknowledgement and the kept turns. The original counts the full initial chat history built around them, which includes its startup context.
Truncated tool output is not saved to a file, and the character limit is a fixed parameter instead of the smaller of a setting and the remaining context.
The summariser is any function you pass in. The original's system prompt, with its required snapshot sections and its rule to ignore instructions in the history, is not included.
The two instructions sent to the summariser are shortened paraphrases of the original's; they keep the same requests, including repeating the snapshot unchanged when nothing is missing.
The summariser always receives the truncated older history; the original sends the untruncated version when it fits in the model's limit.
No hooks, telemetry or chat recording, and no experimental context-management path.
